spec_match.rationale: Demonstrates the Selectors Level 4 invalid-selector-list rule as it applies to adopting :navigation-source, and the forgiving-list escape hatch (:is()), both measured against the real parser via cssRules counts and getComputedStyle.

interactive.rationale: Live measurement on load plus a re-measure button, and a real fix/unfix toggle that rewrites rule A's stylesheet text and re-measures — the before/after is executed, not narrated.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card promises three live-measured stylesheets showing failure, safe split, and :is() escape hatch; delivered exactly.

edge_cases.rationale: This page IS the edge case; it also distinguishes parse survival from rendered effect per rule and handles the future state (all three passing on 156+) with dedicated summary wording.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/6327898878377984, the css-navigation-1 anchor, and the selectors-4 forgiving-selector definition.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite's stylesheet-rule-survives assertion is the 156 contract for the same mechanism; this page additionally shows the failure mode the suite's fail branch corresponds to today.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chromium 141 measured live exactly the documented gotcha: rule A 0 rules survived / span unstyled, rules B and C 1 rule / outline rendered (console log '[navsrc:gotcha] measured {A:{survived:0,applied:false},B:{survived:1,applied:true},C:{survived:1,applied:true}}'); the :is() rewrite flipped A to applied and the restore flipped it back, verified via scripted clicks. Unlike the sibling pages this page's primary claim is fully observable pre-156; screenshots captured at both viewports with clean console. (Verification tooling: headless Chromium CLI + scripted Playwright; chrome-devtools-mcp unavailable in this environment.)

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts gotcha-measured with the full outcome matrix, safe-patterns-survive as a real pass/fail contract, and fix-applied on the rewrite branch.

design_system.rationale: Outline colours from accent variables, verdict text paired with colour, both action buttons inherit the correct global button colours, tables in a scroller.

accessibility.rationale: Summary is role=status aria-live=polite; results are a table with row/column headers and textual verdicts; specimen code blocks are tabindex=0; all buttons ≥44px and keyboard operable.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: scrollWidth 360 at 360×740 DPR3 (the three code specimens scroll inside their own pre containers); measured table and buttons wrap cleanly; desktop 1280×800 screenshot shows the full matrix without clipping.

openQuestions.title: Confirm the all-three-survive summary on a Chrome 156+ build
openQuestions.detail: The summary distinguishes 'selector parsed natively' from ':is() rewrite active' via a live CSS.supports probe; the native branch could not be observed on Chromium 141. On Chrome Canary ≥156 confirm the load-time measurement reports all three rules applied with the native wording.

guidanceConsulted.query: progressive enhancement unsupported CSS selector fallback feature detection
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Never let an experimental selector share a top-level selector list with production rules; use :is()/:where() or separate rules for safe adoption.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The page is a live demonstration of exactly this recommendation, and the other three concept pages keep every :navigation-source rule standalone, which this page cites.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible loading progress status announcements live region
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Announce re-measurements via a polite live region and keep results in semantic tables.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Summary output is aria-live=polite with an action prefix per re-measure; the results matrix is a real table with scoped headers.

summary: The adoption-hazard page, and the one concept fully provable on today's browsers: the comma-poisoned rule measurably dies (0 rules, unstyled span) while the split and :is() variants survive, with a working live fix/restore toggle. Verified interactively on Chromium 141 at both viewports with a clean console.
